I've been farming these 9.5 mu for 35 years, and I know every plot like the back of my hand. My old man and I used to do everything together, but now it's mostly me and my son's family — three mouths to feed, so I can't afford to mess up a season. I went to middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags, but honestly I learn more from watching what works in the fields around me than from any book.

My cropping system is cotton — that's my main crop and my main income. This year I will plant **5 mu of cotton**. I use Guoxinmian, a hybrid variety. The seed costs me about 45 yuan per mu, and I plant about 3 jin per mu. For fertilizer, I will put down one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu as basal — the one with 22-9-9 on the bag, which is about 11 jin of nitrogen, 4.5 jin of phosphorus, and 4.5 jin of potassium per mu. Then when the plants start flowering, I will topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, which adds another 11.5 jin of nitrogen. I know that is a lot of nitrogen, but cotton is hungry, and I would rather spend an extra 30 yuan per mu on fertilizer than lose half my yield to poor bolls. My neighbor Li Sao used less last year and her cotton was stunted — I am not making that mistake. Total that comes to about **18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu**. I will irrigate 3 times from my well: once at planting, once at flowering, and once at boll filling. Cotton pests are terrible around here — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — so I will spray 12 times total, starting in June. I do rotary tillage every spring to break up the soil. I expect about 550 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather cooperates.

I also have **2.5 mu of cauliflower** that I grow in spring. I buy improved seedlings from the dealer in town — about 2,500 plants per mu at 100 yuan per mu. Cauliflower needs a lot of food to make big tight heads. I put down 100 jin of 18-18-18 compound as basal, and then topdress twice with 80 jin each time of a high-potassium compound. That works out to about **20 kg nitrogen, 12 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu**. I irrigate 4 times because cauliflower wilts fast if it gets dry, and I spray pesticides 5 times for cabbage worms and aphids. Rotary tillage, same as everything else. I should get about 4,500 kg per mu of fresh heads if I time the harvest right before the market floods.

The last **2 mu is stevia**. I started this about five years ago after the buyer came to our village offering 6 yuan per jin for dried leaves. I buy improved seedlings — about 8,000 plants per mu — and that costs me about 300 yuan per mu, which hurts, but the returns are steady. Stevia doesn't need as much nitrogen as cotton or the stems get too long and leafy, but it still needs feeding. I put down 100 jin of 18-12-18 compound as basal, and then topdress with 120 jin of balanced compound split into two applications. That is about **18 kg nitrogen, 12 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potassium per mu**. I irrigate 4 times and spray pesticides 7 times. I harvest once in August and dry the leaves in my yard. I expect about 500 kg per mu of dried leaves.

Everything connects in my head. The cotton and stevia seedlings go in around mid-April when the soil warms up. The cauliflower seedlings go in a bit earlier, late March. My well is good, but pumping costs diesel, so every irrigation is a decision. I keep my own books — fertilizer is my biggest cash cost this year, probably 1,200 to 1,500 yuan total. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and sleep easy than lie awake worrying about yellow plants. That is how I have always done it, and so far it has kept food on the table.
